items.title: Daemons can now send traces to Vercel Tracing
items.text: can now send OpenTelemetry traces to , allowing you and your agents to inspect background worker operations alongside the rest of your project's traces.Vercel DaemonsVercel Tracing Vercel provides each daemon with a Unix socket for receiving OTLP/HTTP traces and sets the socket's path in .VERCEL_OTEL_SOCKET_PATH Upgrading to version 2.3.0 or later enables automatic trace export for Node.js daemons using the default configuration. The SDK detects this socket and sends the spans your worker records to Vercel.@vercel/otel These spans are available through the , which can search by service name within a project and return JSON for your agents.Vercel CLI Learn more in the .daemon tracing documentation Read more

items.title: Token Pass now includes $150 in tokens for $30/month
items.text: now includes $150 of tokens per month (up from $80) for the same $30 per team per month.Vercel Token Pass The credit applies to featured open-weight models served through , including Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1 Pro, GLM 5.3, GLM 5.3 Flash, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.AI Gateway Credit resets each billing period with no rollover. When it runs out, requests using standard AI Gateway keys or OIDC tokens fall back to the team's AI Gateway balance, while requests using Token Pass-scoped keys stop with no overage charges. Token Pass is an Early Access add-on for Pro teams, with limited spots and a waitlist when they fill. To connect your coding agent, run in the Vercel CLI, or use a Token Pass API key if your agent supports AI Gateway.vercel token-pass Subscribe to Token Pass in your .AI Gateway dashboard Read more

items.title: Vercel Security Review no longer requires a linked Vercel project
items.text: You can now scan code changes for vulnerabilities with in GitHub repositories that have not yet been linked to a Vercel project.Vercel Security Review By default, Security Review covers all unlinked repositories the Vercel GitHub App can access in a connected GitHub account. You can limit coverage to selected connected accounts or individual repositories in Agent settings. Once enabled, each push to a covered repository automatically triggers a review of its code changes. Security Review checks commits directly in repositories with Security Review enabled, without requiring a Vercel project or deployment. When a push creates a deployment for a linked project with Security Review enabled, the review uses the additional project and deployment context. Connect the account in your team’s , then enable Security Review in .Git settingsVercel Agent settings Get started with the .Security Review documentation Read more

items.title: Vercel Sandbox starts up to 4x faster
items.text: now initializes up to 4x faster outside the Washington, D.C. () region when reused image data is served from a regional cache.Vercel Sandboxiad1 Initialization now reads cached image data close to where the sandbox runs, avoiding round trips to origin image storage in on cache hits. Regional caching supports managed and custom images backed by Vercel Container Registry, including snapshots based on those images.iad1 In internal end-to-end benchmarks with , startup time fell about 75% in Paris and from about 3.5s to 1.05s in Seoul. Regions closer to origin storage generally see smaller improvements because requests already travel a shorter distance.Vercel Managed Images Learn more in the .Vercel Sandbox documentation Read more

items.title: Build cache size limit on Vercel increased to 5 GB
items.text: The size limit on all has been increased to 5 GB. This allows projects to save more installed dependencies and framework files for reuse between deployments, which can reduce install and build times.build cacheVercel build machines Build machines are the compute environments that install dependencies and build your project before deployment. Previously, caches were discarded if they exceeded 1.5 GB on Basic and Standard, 3 GB on Enhanced, or 4.75 GB on Turbo, leaving the next build without a cache. The change applies automatically across all build machine types at no additional charge, with no configuration required. Learn more in the .build cache documentation Read more
